name: Standing Pies
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: quarters of a pint of water
ingredients.originalText: three quarters of a pint of water

instructions.text: Cut up the butter and put it into a sauce-pan with water
Cover it and set it on hot coals
Have ready two pounds of sifted flour in a pan and make a hole in the middle
Pour in the melted butter as soon as it boils
Gradually mix in the flour with a spoon
When well mixed, knead it with your hands into a stiff dough
Sprinkle your paste-board with flour and lay the dough upon it
Continue to knead it with your hands till it no longer sticks and is quite light
Let it stand an hour to cool
Cut off pieces for the bottom and top and roll them out thick
Roll out a long piece for the sides or walls and fix it on the bottom to stand up all round
Cement them together with white of egg, pinching and closing firmly
Put in the ingredients of your pie
Lay on the lid or top crust, pinching the edges closely together
Ornament the sides and top with leaves or flowers of paste shaped with a tin cutter
Notch or scollop the edges handsomely
Glaze it all over with white of egg

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Cut up the butter and put it into a sauce-pan with water
2. Cover it and set it on hot coals
3. Have ready two pounds of sifted flour in a pan and make a hole in the middle
4. Pour in the melted butter as soon as it boils
5. Gradually mix in the flour with a spoon
6. When well mixed, knead it with your hands into a stiff dough
7. Sprinkle your paste-board with flour and lay the dough upon it
8. Continue to knead it with your hands till it no longer sticks and is quite light
9. Let it stand an hour to cool
10. Cut off pieces for the bottom and top and roll them out thick
11. Roll out a long piece for the sides or walls and fix it on the bottom to stand up all round
12. Cement them together with white of egg, pinching and closing firmly
13. Put in the ingredients of your pie
14. Lay on the lid or top crust, pinching the edges closely together
15. Ornament the sides and top with leaves or flowers of paste shaped with a tin cutter
16. Notch or scollop the edges handsomely
17. Glaze it all over with white of egg
18. Bake it four hours
